title: Michelangelo
objective: After this level you can describe the David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
summary: Michelangelo carved the David (1501-04) from an abandoned block, showing David before the fight. A sculptor at heart, he then painted the Sistine ceiling standing up.

cards.headline: Florence owned a giant block of marble that nobody could use.
cards.body: Two earlier sculptors had started on it and rejected it for its flaws, and it lay abandoned for about 25 years. In 1501 the job went to a 26-year-old named Michelangelo.

cards.headline: David, before the fight
cards.body: By 1504 the block had become a marble nude 5.17 metres tall: weight on one leg, a sling so slim you can barely see it, watchful eyes. Earlier Florentine artists showed David triumphant over Goliath. Michelangelo's is usually read as David before the battle, concentrating. A committee that included Leonardo set him up in Florence's main square as a symbol of the republic's liberty.

cards.headline: A sculptor on a ceiling
cards.body: Pope Julius II then put him to work on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. Michelangelo thought of himself as a sculptor, and he'd never painted a fresco. He did it anyway, from 1508 to 1512, standing upright on scaffolding he designed himself. The famous picture of him lying on his back is a myth, probably from a 1965 film.

cards.fact: In the Creation of Adam, two fingers almost touch.
cards.context: Nine scenes from Genesis run down the middle of the ceiling. In the Creation of Adam, Adam lounges on the ground and lifts a limp hand, while God, carried by angels in swirling drapery, reaches toward him. Their fingertips nearly meet, but not quite. All the drama lives in that sliver of empty space.

questions.prompt: Which moment is Michelangelo's David usually read as showing?

options.label: David standing over Goliath's head
options.rationale: That's how earlier Florentine artists showed him.

options.label: David crowned as king
options.rationale: He holds a sling, not a crown.

options.label: David resting after the fight
options.rationale: He's usually read as concentrating before it.

questions.explanation: Unlike earlier triumphant Davids, Michelangelo's is usually read as David before the battle, concentrating.

questions.prompt: Put these moments in Michelangelo's story in order, from earliest to latest.
items: The block had become a marble nude
The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel
questions.explanation: In 1501 the marble block went to the 26-year-old Michelangelo, by 1504 it was David, from 1508 to 1512 he painted the Sistine ceiling, and the lying-on-his-back myth probably comes from a 1965 film.

questions.prompt: In the Creation of Adam, the gap where the fingers of God and Adam don't quite touch is, in Level 3's terms, _____.

options.label: a vanishing point
options.rationale: That's where parallel lines meet in perspective.

options.label: implied texture
options.rationale: Texture is how a surface seems to feel.

options.label: a secondary color
options.rationale: Secondaries are mixes of two primaries.

questions.explanation: The empty space between the fingers is negative space, and it has a shape of its own.
